## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "rich/cells.py", "content": "from __future__ import annotations

import re
from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Callable

from ._cell_widths import CELL_WIDTHS

# Regex to match sequence of the most common character ranges
_is_single_cell_widths = re.compile("^[\u0020-\u006f\u00a0\u02ff\u0370-\u0482]*$").match


@lru_cache(4096)
def cached_cell_len(text: str) -> int:
    """Get the number of cells required to display text.

    This method always caches, which may use up a lot of memory. It is recommended to use
    `cell_len` over this method.

    Args:
        text (str): Text to display.

    Returns:
        int: Get the number of cells required to display text.
    """
    _get_size = get_character_cell_size
    total_size = sum(_get_size(character) for character in text)
    return total_size


def cell_len(text: str, _cell_len: Callable[[str], int] = cached_cell_len) -> int:
    """Get the number of cells required to display text.

    Args:
        text (str): Text to display.

    Returns:
        int: Get the number of cells required to display text.
    """
    if len(text) < 512:
        return _cell_len(text)
    _get_size = get_character_cell_size
    total_size = sum(_get_size(character) for character in text)
    return total_size


@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def get_character_cell_size(character: str) -> int:
    """Get the cell size of a character.

    Args:
        character (str): A single character.

    Returns:
        int: Number of cells (0, 1 or 2) occupied by that character.
    """
    return _get_codepoint_cell_size(ord(character))


@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def _get_codepoint_cell_size(codepoint: int) -> int:
    """Get the cell size of a character.

    Args:
        codepoint (int): Codepoint of a character.

    Returns:
        int: Number of cells (0, 1 or 2) occupied by that character.
    """

    _table = CELL_WIDTHS
    lower_bound = 0
    upper_bound = len(_table) - 1
    index = (lower_bound + upper_bound) // 2
    while True:
        start, end, width = _table[index]
        if codepoint < start:
            upper_bound = index - 1
        elif codepoint > end:
            lower_bound = index + 1
        else:
            return 0 if width == -1 else width
        if upper_bound < lower_bound:
            break
        index = (lower_bound + upper_bound) // 2
    return 1


def set_cell_size(text: str, total: int) -> str:
    """Set the length of a string to fit within given number of cells."""

    if _is_single_cell_widths(text):
        size = len(text)
        if size < total:
            return text + " " * (total - size)
        return text[:total]

    if total <= 0:
        return ""
    cell_size = cell_len(text)
    if cell_size == total:
        return text
    if cell_size < total:
        return text + " " * (total - cell_size)

    start = 0
    end = len(text)

    # Binary search until we find the right size
    while True:
        pos = (start + end) // 2
        before = text[: pos + 1]
        before_len = cell_len(before)
        if before_len == total + 1 and cell_len(before[-1]) == 2:
            return before[:-1] + " "
        if before_len == total:
            return before
        if before_len > total:
            end = pos
        else:
            start = pos


def chop_cells(
    text: str,
    width: int,
) -> list[str]:
    """Split text into lines such that each line fits within the available (cell) width.

    Args:
        text: The text to fold such that it fits in the given width.
        width: The width available (number of cells).

    Returns:
        A list of strings such that each string in the list has cell width
        less than or equal to the available width.
    """
    _get_character_cell_size = get_character_cell_size
    lines: list[list[str]] = [[]]

    append_new_line = lines.append
    append_to_last_line = lines[-1].append

    total_width = 0

    for character in text:
        cell_width = _get_character_cell_size(character)
        char_doesnt_fit = total_width + cell_width > width
